coordinate_contract.space: vault space: model units, x east, y up, z south; the model FRONT is the north face (-z); the floor is y = 0
coordinate_contract.root: the vault block's floor centre, i.e. model point (8, 0, 8); every display entity is spawned at the root with yaw 0 and transform-only facing (see composition)
coordinate_contract.display_origin: an item display draws its model centred on the entity, so model point (8, 8, 8) sits at root + (0, 0.5, 0) blocks: the rest translation of every persistent piece is (0, 0.5, 0); its rest rotation SENT is rotY(180) = (0, 1, 0, 0) xyzw (the client's own half turn then cancels it, so the model stands in vault space: front north)
coordinate_contract.display_transform: none (the item display default, no display override in the model JSON)

hinge.positive_direction: positive rotation about +x lifts the lid's FRONT edge (opens); angle = lid.rot_x_deg

coordinate_contract.client_item_display_flip: Minecraft's item display renderer turns the item MODEL a half circle about y inside its own frame, after the transformation: the client draws T + q (F v) with F = rotY(180). At identity the model's north face looks south (verified in a real 1.21.1 client). The flip acts on the model only, not on the translation.
coordinate_contract.composition: Intended pose = Rnet (Tc + R v). For the lid Tc = H + R(c - H), R = rotX(lid.rot_x_deg), H = hinge (root-local blocks), c = (0, 0.5, 0); that is root x translate(H) x R x translate(-H) x rest, no second offset anywhere. Other pieces: Tc = c (+ (0, 0, press/16) for face_plate), R = identity. All get + (root.x_units/16, 0, 0) first. Rnet = rotY(facing_yaw_deg) (north 0, west 90, south 180, east -90). SENT to the client: translation T = Rnet Tc, left rotation q = Rnet R F with F = rotY(180) (so the client's own F cancels); entity yaw stays 0.
coordinate_contract.interpolation: every tick the server sends the sampled transformation with interpolation_duration = 1 tick (one sample per tick, so rotation about the hinge follows the arc instead of cutting the chord)

reveal_a.origin: authored centred at (8, 8, 8): a display entity rotates it about its own middle

vault_full.note: static assembled closed model (body + lid + face_plate + candy_fill); NOT used at runtime

root.x_units.drives: every persistent piece, x (in vault space, before facing)

ease: the ease on a key shapes the segment that starts at that key: linear, in_quad, out_quad, in_cubic, out_cubic, in_out_sine

closed_idle.note: A barely visible breath: the lid lifts 0.35 degrees and settles. First and last frame are the closed pose.

anticipation.note: The whole vault trembles (root x shake) while the lid rattles. Ends exactly closed.

unlock.note: The plate clicks in 0.6 unit and springs back; the latch pops the lid up 1.5 degrees.

open.note: The lid swings to the final angle, overshoots it by 3 degrees at tick 10 and settles at tick 14.

open_hold.note: The lid rests open; a 0.4 degree sway keeps it alive. Loops until close is requested.

close.note: The lid falls, shuts at tick 11 with a 1.8 degree bounce, the plate clicks, all settled closed at tick 14.

reset.note: Instant: every channel to its rest value, reveal candy removed. Allowed from every state.

state_machine.start: CLOSED -> ANTICIPATING (outcome treat or trick is fixed here and does not change the pose timeline)
state_machine.close: OPEN -> CLOSING (requested by the controller: the close_request event, or an API call)
state_machine.reset: any state -> CLOSED, all channels to rest, reveal candy removed (sequence 'reset')

reveal.note: Floating reveal candy: each is its own display entity, spawned only after the lid is fully OPEN (after OPENING), so the trick and treat timelines are identical until then. Position = root + start + rise; rotation yaw spin; scale from scale_keys.
